model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) percentage for five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ to 10³. The y-axis represents ACC (%) on a linear scale from 40 to 65. The Base method, shown as a dark gray line with circle markers, starts at approximately 38% ACC at a co-occurrence number of 1 and increases slightly to about 44% at 1000. The MEND method, depicted as a brown line with diamond markers, begins at around 44% ACC at a co-occurrence number of 1 and rises to approximately 57% at 1000. The FT method, represented by a blue line with triangle markers, starts at about 40% ACC at a co-occurrence number of 1 and increases to roughly 48% at 1000. The MEMIT method, shown as a purple line with star markers, begins at approximately 44% ACC at a co-occurrence number of 1, peaks at around 51% at 100, and then slightly declines to about 55% at 1000. The ROME method, indicated by a green line with square markers, starts at about 51% ACC at a co-occurrence number of 1 and steadily increases to approximately 66% at 1000.
